messages:
Alyssa (Account Executive): Quick sync — Acme just agreed to a 30d POC. Need a quick throughput/provisioning plan + answers for pricing and the security questionnaire. They provided traffic: steady 12 rps, peak 25 rps sustained for 20m, occasional 90 rps bursts for ~3m. Latency SLO target p95 <200ms. Any immediate blockers?

Jin (Sales Engineer): Model detail? small LLM or larger instruct-tuned? quantized variants? That changes GPU counts a lot.

Alyssa (Account Executive): They said using an open-llm base (~13B) for chat completions. Will test a quantized 4-bit checkpoint if we recommend it.

Ravi (Solutions Architect): Ok — rough calc: baseline 12 rps @13B non-quantized -> roughly 1 x A100 equivalent for 12 rps with batching; peaks 25 rps => need either autoscale to +1 instance or reserve 2x capacity. For 90 rps bursts we need prewarm/burst capacity or fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant.

Marta (SRE): Agree. Two ops patterns:
- Reserved approach: reserve 2 GPU slots (dedicated) with autoscale floor at 1 and ceiling 3. Preheat pool for bursts (3-5 nodes warm). This gives near-zero coldstart for that 3m burst.
- Hosted/spot: keep 1 reserved, allow burst to shared capacity with fallback routing to quantized v2 model. Expect higher tail latency during burst.

Jin (Sales Engineer): To quantify cost and latency we need queue depth and token distribution. They gave avg payload ~1k tokens, worst-case 5k tokens. That increases per-request GPU time a lot.

Alyssa (Account Executive): They mentioned many short assistant messages (1k avg), but a small % (~5%) are long generation ~5k.

Marta (SRE): Important: long-tail tokens dominate GPU seconds. Recommendation: enable token budget throttles + early-stop heuristics for POC, and map long requests to reserved pool only. Autoscale policy suggestion:
- scale up when avg GPU utilization > 70% for 30s
- scale down when < 35% for 2m
- maintain 2 prewarm slots for burst handling

Ravi (Solutions Architect): Also enable prefix KV caching for repeated conversation contexts — 20% token savings seen in similar workloads. Would reduce effective token/time per request.

Jin (Sales Engineer): For pricing: if they pick Dedicated reserved 2-GPU slots with burst headroom to 3 for 30 days, we should present: monthly reserved fee + usage overage for burst GPU minutes. Priya can we ballpark margin-friendly quote?

Priya (Finance): Quick ballpark: reserved 2x GPUs (A100-equivalent) monthly commit -> $Xk/month (I'll fill exact). Burst minutes billed at 1.5x normal per-minute rate. Quantized model serving is ~30% cheaper on GPU time; include that as an optional savings line. I'll produce a detailed quote after we agree on expected baseline RPS and token mix.

Alyssa (Account Executive): Security questionnaire status? They need encryption-at-rest, KMS integration, and SOC2 attestation fields answered before contract.

sec-bot (security-bot): Security questionnaire: "KMS integrated" = yes (customer-managed keys available), "SOC2 status" = Type II in 2024, "VPC/Private deployment" = available via Redwood Private; see https://internal.redwood/security/poc-answers (internal link).

Marta (SRE): Operational notes for POC runbook:
1) Run internal loadgen sim for token distribution:
```
./loadgen --rps 12 --burst 90 --dist long:5% --tokens-avg 1000 --tokens-long 5000 --duration 2h
```
2) Start with dedicated 2-GPU reserve, autoscale ceiling 3, prewarm 2 slots.
3) Route long requests to reserved-only queue with higher cost flag.
4) Observe p95 latency and GPU util; adjust scale thresholds.

Jin (Sales Engineer): Fallback plan if we hit capacity issues: rollback to quantized-4bit variant (expected +10-30% latency but 2-3x throughput), and traffic-shed long jobs (notify customer). Implement fallback routing policy: region -> reserved pool -> quantized pool -> degrade to rate-limit.

Alyssa (Account Executive): Awesome. Two asks for me to take to Acme: 1) Confirm token mix (we have 2h to confirm), 2) confirm willingness to accept quantized variant for bursts.

Priya (Finance): I'll draft the quote (reserved 2-GPU + burst ceiling) and include a line for quantized-cost-savings. ETA 24h.

Ravi (Solutions Architect): I'll spin up an internal sim with Marta tomorrow morning and post results (latency/Coverage heatmap).

Marta (SRE): I'll prepare the autoscale policy template and the preheat config, plus runbook steps for on-call.

Alyssa (Account Executive): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with Acme and paste token confirmation here. :thumbsup:
